preconditions.expression: T == int(stdin.split()[0]) and T >= 1 and T <= 10
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(S) >= 1 and len(S) <= 1000 and all(c in {'0', '1'} for c in S) for S in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:T+1]])
preconditions.description: Each of the T test cases is a single line containing a binary string S of length N (1 ≤ N ≤ 1000), where S consists only of '0' and '1'.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '\n'.join(str(len(equivalence_classes(S))) for S in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:T+1]])
postconditions.description: For each test case string S, the output is a line containing the number of distinct equivalence classes of all non-empty substrings of S, where two substrings A and B are equivalent (A ~ B) if they have the same length and A can be transformed into B by zero or more operations of reversing substrings containing an even number of '1's.

postconditions.expression: all(len(equivalence_classes(S)) >= 1 for S in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:T+1]])
postconditions.description: The number of equivalence classes is at least 1 for any non-empty string S, since a string is trivially equivalent to itself.
